content: {"id": "0ef03270-9f3e-4025-a518-94ca5580e1e7", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "What is the difference between an Application Load Balancer and a Network Load Balancer?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "8ef5489a-2db0-4c57-8479-6b2c3cd2cea0", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Both are Elastic Load Balancing types. The main difference is the network layer each works at.

| | **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** | **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TLS, TCP_UDP |
| **Routing** | Content-based. It routes on path, host header, HTTP headers, query strings, methods, and source IP. | Connection-based. It routes on IP, port, and protocol. |
| **Performance** | Good, with request-level processing overhead | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency. It handles millions of requests per second and sudden traffic spikes. |
| **IP addresses** | Dynamic. You use its DNS name. | One static IP per AZ, and you can attach Elastic IPs. It also supports PrivateLink. |
| **Client IP preservation** | Passed in the `X-Forwarded-For` header | Preserved natively for instance targets |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023). Older NLBs may not have one attached. |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions | Instances, IPs, ALBs |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS and supports SNI. It also supports authentication through Cognito or OIDC. | Can terminate TLS, or pass encrypted traffic through to the targets |
| **Other features** | WAF integration, redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups | Works with PrivateLink and handles non-HTTP protocols |

**Choose an ALB when:**
- You run HTTP/HTTPS web apps, microservices, or APIs.
- You need path-based or host-based routing, for example `/api` to one service and `/web` to another.
- You want WAF, user authentication, or Lambda targets.

**Choose an NLB when:**
- You need extreme performance or very low latency.
- You use non-HTTP protocols such as gaming, IoT, MQTT, or custom TCP/UDP.
- You need static or Elastic IPs, for example for customer firewall allow-listing.
- You want to expose a service through PrivateLink.

You can also put an NLB in front of an ALB. That gives you static IPs and PrivateLink, along with Layer 7 routing.

If you'd like, I can look at the load balancers in your connected AWS accounts and tell you which type each one uses.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
